what_happened: The job was meant to make a model usage limit a hold instead of a job failure. It was rejected at the final verdict. One major finding was listed, and no acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no checks as failed. The finding: the drain still stops with "repeated failure" when the usage limit is hit while it reads a request. Reading a request is the first model call the drain makes for each queued item. The hold handling was added on other paths (probably the producer and verifier calls), but the reading path (reading.rs:483, drain.rs:798-809, 1075) still treats the limit as an ordinary failure.
cause: Nothing lists every place in the code that makes a model call, so a change meant to apply to all model calls is checked only at the places the producer thought of. The usage-limit signal is handled by call site, not once at the shared point where model errors are classified. The reading step has its own error path into the drain's failure counter. Only the verifier's read at the final verdict compares the change against all call sites, and there rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the producer's work or the reading's criteria.
prevention: Classify the usage-limit error once, at the single point where model-call errors are turned into results, as a typed "hold" outcome. Every caller (reading, planning, critic, producer, verifier) must receive that type, and the drain's failure counter must not count it. Add a test that injects the limit error at each model-call stage, with reading first, and asserts the drain holds and the failure count stays unchanged. Require the reading to list each stage that calls the model as a criterion.
proposed_request: Make a model usage limit a hold at every model-call stage of the queue drain, not only some. Outcome: when the usage limit is hit while reading a request, planning, criticising, producing or verifying, the drain pauses the item as a hold, does not count it toward "repeated failure", and resumes the item when the limit lifts. Classify the limit error in one shared place so all stages get the same typed hold result. Acceptance: (1) for each stage, including the request-reading step in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and the failure handling in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, a test injects the usage-limit error and asserts the item is held, the failure count is unchanged and the drain does not stop; (2) a test shows an ordinary non-limit error at the reading step still counts as a failure; (3) the change description lists every model-call stage and the test that covers it; (4) the existing checks pass.
